content.thinking:
This intervention leans heavily on warmth and community narrative — framing climate scientists as neighbors helping in disasters — which should hit benevolence and integrity hard while also touching competence through the "models save lives" angle. Given its vivid, non-political framing that lowers reactance for conservatives, I'd estimate this as one of the stronger arms, around 2.8 on trust_multidimensional.

Working through the secondary outcomes: distrust drops modestly (~-1.3), funding perceptions barely shift since the message doesn't touch funding directly (~0.8), while policy_role_mean gets a solid boost (~1.8) since the narrative explicitly shows scientists collaborating with emergency managers. Institutional trust and belief measures move only slightly given dilution across many outcomes, concern and behavior nudge up from the storm/wildfire risk salience, and the AMS donation/newsletter signals stay small but positive given the meteorological society framing.

parsed_output.reasoning_summary: This arm is a vivid, multi-page narrative that humanizes climate scientists as neighbors, parents, and first-responder collaborators, with concrete life-saving episodes (Harvey flood maps, 2020 wildfire models). Mechanistically it targets the benevolence and integrity dimensions of the trust battery most directly, with a secondary competence signal (useful, actionable science), and it is deliberately non-partisan and shared-values framed, which minimizes reactance among skeptics — the group with the most headroom. I therefore place it toward the upper end of the plausible trust range (~+2.7 on the fresh multidimensional battery), with the re-asked single trust item shrunk by anchoring (~+1.7) and a smaller mirrored reduction in distrust (distrust items are stickier and less symmetric). Because the text depicts scientists working hand-in-hand with emergency managers and local officials, policy_role_mean should move appreciably (~+1.7), while institutional trust is diluted by the federal-government item (~+0.9). Belief, concern, and policy support are distal and only indirectly touched by the extreme-weather imagery, so all sit under ~1 point; behavioral intentions lower still. Incentivized outcomes get near-floor values, with a small nudge for the AMS donation because meteorologists are explicitly praised in the text.
